teaching.hint: Addition begins at the least significant place; how can each forward-order list expose that place without changing its links?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Forward-order lists hide the least significant digits at their ends, so auxiliary last-in-first-out storage can expose the needed addition order without mutating either input.
solution_outline.approach: Traverse both lists and store their digits in stacks. Pop available digits with a carry, create the current sum digit, and place that node before the already-built result until both stacks and the carry are empty.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The stack tops are the next unprocessed digits at the same decimal place; the carry comes exactly from processed less-significant places, and the current result already represents those places in forward order.
solution_outline.correctness: Each iteration performs the standard decimal addition for one aligned place and updates the carry correctly. Placing its digit before the accumulated less-significant suffix keeps the result in forward order. When inputs and carry are exhausted, every place, including any new leading carry, has been represented exactly once.
solution_outline.complexity: For input lengths m and n, the traversal and pops take O(m + n) time and the stacks use O(m + n) auxiliary space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Reversing input links can violate the follow-up's no-reversal intent and may unexpectedly mutate caller-owned lists.

accepted_alternatives: Recursion that descends to aligned least-significant positions and propagates carries while constructing the result on unwinding, with O(m + n) call-stack space.
common_wrong_turns: Adding forward nodes before reaching the least significant digits
Assuming the lists have equal length
source_fidelity_notes: Examples and image were omitted; forward digit order, nonempty nonnegative inputs, leading-zero rule, digit and length bounds, returned representation, and no-reversal follow-up were retained.
